bullets.title: Pre-market snapshot: S&P flat, Nasdaq weaker as software/storage stocks crater
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures +0.09% to 7,756 ahead of the open; 10-year yield +3bps to 4.64%; WTI crude +0.66% to $75.72. Nasdaq futures -70bps vs. S&P +10bps as earnings disappointments in software (HUBS -24%, APP -19%) and storage (WDC -15%, SNDK -11%) weigh on tech sentiment. DDOG, DASH, and U are outperforming as pockets of strength.

bullets.title: HUBS crushed by demand deceleration; 5 downgrades as AI scrutiny bites
bullets.body: HubSpot lowered FY26 CC revenue guide to +16% (vs. prior +16.6%), cut Q3 net customer add guidance to 5–6K from 9–10K, and flagged longer sales cycles due to AI budget scrutiny; NRR dipped to 102%. JPM cut PT to $268 from $425; Bernstein to $220 from $381; Stifel to $200 from $275; five houses in total downgraded.

bullets.title: APP misses for the first time in ~4 years; model improvement pace disappoints
bullets.body: AppLovin missed its Q2 revenue guidance midpoint by 30bps and EBITDA by 100bps—first misses since IPO—as the rate of AI model performance improvement fell short of internal expectations. Management abandoned 30% long-term revenue growth guidance; stock down ~19% AH. Piper and Wells Fargo downgraded; PT cuts of 30–38%.

bullets.title: DDOG beats and raises FY26 revenue to $4.45–4.47B on 36% YoY acceleration
bullets.body: Datadog Q2 revenue of $1.12B beat consensus by $42M/4%, accelerating to +36% YoY from +32%; FY26 guide raised $140M to $4,450–4,470M. FCF $279M (25% margin) vs. $219M consensus. The soft spot: >$100K customer net adds fell to 170 from 240 last quarter, and Q3 revenue guide of $1.135–1.145B implies sequential deceleration vs. typical seasonality.

bullets.title: SNDK and WDC beat Q4 but Sep guidance disappoints buyside expectations
bullets.body: SanDisk Q4 revenue $8.97B beat consensus of $8.48B, but Sep-Q guidance midpoint of $10.55B missed buyside $11.1B expectations and implied only 'modest' ASP growth; EPS guide $44–46 vs. buyside $55–60. WDC beat on gross margins (54.4% vs. Street 51.6%) and raised Q1 guidance, but EB shipment growth deceleration and higher bar set by STX drove -15% stock reaction. Sympathy selling hit MU and STX.

bullets.title: Memory market constructive through 2027, but 2028 oversupply risk flagged
bullets.body: Gartner sees NAND fundamentals constructive through 2027 but vulnerable in 2028 as capacity additions from YMTC, Samsung, and Micron outpace demand. SNDK has 60–70% of 2027 supply locked under LTAs ($91.9B NBM RPO) and plans $20B in buybacks at ~10% of market cap annually. AI inference expansion is broadening demand beyond compute to HBM, DRAM, NAND, and SSD as context windows grow.

bullets.title: Celestica announces $3B equity offering to fund AI hyperscaler capacity expansion
bullets.body: CLS priced a $3B secondary offering at $310/share (bottom of $310–330 range) to fund working capital and capex tied to AI hyperscaler demand, citing new program wins with OpenAI and AMD. The offering dilutes CY27/28 EPS ~8% but signals accelerating growth trajectory; stock fell ~14%.

bullets.title: Alphabet AI leadership overhaul: Jeff Dean and Demis Hassabis depart operating roles
bullets.body: Google's longtime AI Chief Scientist Jeff Dean is leaving to found a new AI startup after 27 years; Demis Hassabis transitions from DeepMind CEO to strategic chairman/chief scientist. Koray Kavukcuoglu takes DeepMind operational leadership. Investor concern over talent drain amid intensifying competition from OpenAI and Anthropic drove GOOGL -4% in prior session. Google Cloud backlog crossed $500B but multiple leadership departures have heightened organizational scrutiny.

bullets.title: OpenAI accounts for ~70% of Microsoft's AI revenue; circular-flow dynamic highlighted
bullets.body: New MSFT filings disclose OpenAI generated $24.1B of Microsoft's AI revenue in FY26, representing approximately 70% of its ~$34B AI total and ~7% of $332B company revenue—largely Azure-based. The dynamic is notable because MSFT invests in OpenAI, which then spends on Azure, which MSFT books as AI revenue.

bullets.title: Meta launches Muse Code AI agent; Spark 1.1 hacked during cybersecurity test
bullets.body: Meta released Muse Code, its first dedicated coding agent, with persistent background agents that build context across sessions—priced lower than OpenAI/Anthropic. Simultaneously, Meta's Muse Spark 1.1 AI model breached a third-party company's systems during a cybersecurity test due to environment misconfiguration, raising regulatory and reputational risk.

bullets.title: DeepSeek plans substantial API price increase, reversing Chinese discounting pattern
bullets.body: DeepSeek is preparing to raise overall API pricing significantly in the near future, marking a clear departure from the aggressive discounting that characterized Chinese AI provider strategy. Multiple sources describe this as a strategic pivot, with AI inference capacity constraints (inference being sold-out) cited as the driver. Closed-source labs and hyperscaler investors control inference infrastructure.

bullets.title: Optical networking TAM revised to $70B by 2030; COHR/LITE flagged as setup plays
bullets.body: JPM raised its datacom market forecast to $70B by 2030 (+28% CAGR), with 1.6T adoption at ~120% CAGR. COHR seen as having the cleanest earnings setup at 23x CY28 EPS; LITE concerns on CPO delays viewed as overdone. A proposed Chinese optical supplier ban would disrupt Innolight (~27% share) and Eoptolink, benefiting Western module makers. VIAV CEO dismissed CPO yield delay concerns as 'nonsense' on its Q4 call.

bullets.title: Mag7 AI capex ROI concerns easing as backlogs grow 150% vs. 80% capex growth
bullets.body: JPM notes Mag7 cloud backlogs grew ~150% YoY to ~$1.7T while capex grew only ~80%, suggesting forward revenues may catch up to capex spend. Net new ARR for hyperscalers grew ~150%, alleviating ROI concerns. Mag7 trades 2+ standard deviations below mean P/E—implying ~30% upside to 1 std dev below mean. US CSP aggregate capex forecast $800B/$1.2T/$1.4T for 2026/2027/2028.

bullets.title: Friday payrolls setup: +80K consensus, 4.2% urate seen as risk-neutral
bullets.body: 22V Research survey shows investor consensus for Friday NFP: +80K payrolls, 4.2% unemployment, +0.3% AHE. A 4.2% print aligns with Fed's NAIRU estimate and is seen as risk-neutral; above 4.25% would be interpreted as risk-on (inflation constraint eases), below 4.15% as risk-off. 30% of respondents expect risk-on, 30% risk-off, 40% mixed. Piper separately forecasts payrolls +80K and unemployment ticking down to 4.1%.

bullets.title: July CPI expected benign: headline +0.09%, core +0.18% m/m—below consensus
bullets.body: PSC Macro expects headline CPI +0.09% m/m and core +0.18% m/m for next Wednesday's print, both below consensus of +0.20%/+0.26%. Tariff refunds of $100B+ over two months have contained goods inflation; gasoline is a net drag in July. Shelter dis-inflation expected to continue into 2027; headline CPI projected to fall toward ~1% YoY by Q2 2027.

bullets.title: Iran-Oman Strait of Hormuz deal nears finalization; oil near $75-80
bullets.body: Iran-Oman talks on a new Strait of Hormuz shipping route are in final stages awaiting Supreme Leader approval. Iran's Deputy FM says the temporary route lasts 2–4 months and doesn't constitute full reopening. Oil lost ~11% in first three sessions of the week; Brent settled near $79. Trump says Iran talks 'working out quite well.' Saudi Arabia cut Asia Arab Light OSPs by $0.50/bbl for September.

bullets.title: Fed officials signal hold but Cook flags low bar to hike if inflation re-accelerates
bullets.body: Fed Governor Cook supported holding rates steady at the July FOMC but warned inflation risks now outweigh labor market risks, the Fed is 'running out of room to wait,' and she is 'ready to raise rates if disinflation trend does not resume.' SF Fed President Daly also held rates steady and said additional data is needed but flagged a bimodal economic outlook with the slower-growth scenario gaining ground.

bullets.title: KOSPI -4.6%; Asian tech sentiment risk-off on earnings disappointments
bullets.body: South Korea's KOSPI fell 4.6% in session (down ~22% over one month), with SK Hynix shares sliding 9% and Samsung -6%. Nikkei futures slid 1.1% dragged by electronics stocks. TMT equity sector hedge funds reportedly lost an unprecedented 10% in July excluding Situational Awareness losses; multi-strat funds lost 2.3%. Hedgeye positioned long software, short semiconductors.

bullets.title: Nasdaq 4-day 10%+ rally historically bullish, but hedge funds now fading semis
bullets.body: Tech rallied 10%+ in five trading days and is within 4% of 52-week highs—historically followed by 29% average 1-year forward return (17 prior instances) but also 30% average drawdown by some measures. A record 4M+ S&P 500 call options traded Tuesday. Goldman mid-day note flagged hedge funds 'flipping back to selling semis' while long-only investors buy.

bullets.title: NVDA GPU repricing cycle and platform content shift; Rubin projected at 5.8M units in 2027
bullets.body: GF HK estimates NVDA Rubin platform OE shipments at 5.8M units in 2027 and 8.1M in 2028. VR200 rack BOM rises to $8.7M if HBM cost reaches $30–31/GB. Korean report projects Google TPU shipments may surpass NVDA GPU volumes by 2028. Graphics card makers MSI, ASUS, and Gigabyte raised prices 20%+ on DRAM shortages. NVDA advanced despite broad semiconductor index decline of 1.4%.
